The shader build emits a reflection sidecar per target, and they are different index spaces for the same source: the SPIR-V pass honours the shader's explicit slots, while the WGSL pass lets Slang auto-number in declaration order and splits a combined Sampler2D into two slots. So the same parameter can be index 0 in one sidecar and index 3 in the other. An index is meaningless without knowing which — a backend that read the wrong sidecar would build a layout that looks entirely plausible and binds the wrong resources.
- **Loom.Graph.ShaderReflection**: The descriptor-bound resource shape of a shader, read from the slangc -reflection-json sidecar that the shader build emits next to each compiled module. Every parameter is recorded with the slot the shader actually gave it (), so a backend builds its descriptor layout from real indices rather than assuming a category order the author had to hand-number to match. The per-category counts remain available as derived views, computed from the same array a layout is built from, so the two cannot disagree. The JSON is target-specific, not shared: see . Which target a reflection was parsed for is carried in and must be checked before its indices are used.
- **Loom.Graph.ShaderReloadRegistry**: Tracks which techniques each shader backs, for hot-reload. A backend records every technique it defines here; when a watched shader artifact changes, the backend maps it to a logical shader name and queues it, and draining (on the render thread) replays each affected technique's descriptor through a backend-supplied redefine callback, bracketed by a GPU drain and a pipeline-cache reset. Pure bookkeeping over neutral descriptors — the file watching, the artifact-name parsing, and the GPU/cache work stay in the backend, behind the callbacks.
- **Loom.Graph.StoreAction**: What happens to an attachment's contents when a pass finishes (the VkRenderingAttachmentInfo.storeOp).
- **Loom.Graph.TechniqueRecord**: A registered technique: the name it was defined under, the descriptor the app declared, and the the backend baked from its shader. A class rather than a struct so a registry lookup on the per-draw path hands back a reference instead of copying.
- **Loom.Graph.TechniqueRegistry**: Every technique defined on an engine, by name. Backend-neutral and device-free, so the record-time checks that consult it are unit-testable without a GPU, and so a technique-name miss reports the same way on every backend rather than once per backend's own exception type. This does not replace a backend's pipeline cache. Those are keyed by baked content (attachment formats, blend state) and stay where they are; this is the one place a name is resolved.
- **Loom.Graph.TechniqueShape**: What a baked technique can accept, in backend-neutral terms — the return of a backend's bake step and the input to the record-time checks. It exists so those checks live once instead of three times: every backend already computes all of this while baking, so returning it costs nothing and, unlike a second accessor the backend must remember to keep in step, it cannot drift from what was actually baked. Every size here is in bytes, matching reflection and the backends' own block constants. A constant buffer holds whatever struct the shader declared — matrices, integers, float4 rows — so a float count is the wrong unit to describe one. That the push API happens to take a ReadOnlySpan<float> is a property of the call, not of the buffer; convert at the call site.
- **Loom.Graph.TimingDecode**: Decodes GPU timestamp readbacks into per-pass timings. Collecting the raw timestamps is backend-specific (a query pool vs a query heap, with different valid-bit masking), but turning begin/end tick pairs into milliseconds and aligning them to the schedule's leaf passes is identical across backends, so it lives here.
- **SUIsei.Animation.AnimationClock**: Advances active storyboards by the per-frame delta. Held by the and stepped once per from its deltaSeconds, so output is fully deterministic: tests tick synthetic deltas and assert the resolved value over time — no frame loop, no GPU. Each active storyboard tracks its own elapsed time; every tick it normalizes each child animation's progress (honouring /// ) and pushes the eased, interpolated value to the target. When an animation finishes, releases the target while leaves the final value in place. A storyboard is dropped once all its children have finished.
- **SUIsei.Animation.AnimationTimeline**: A that drives one target property. The only needs to resolve the target, record where a run starts, push the current value and release the target on stop, so the non-generic base exposes just those seams; the typed value and the apply/release/read delegates live on . The delegates are resolved to typed writes — no reflection, no boxing.
- **SUIsei.Animation.AnimationTimeline`1**: The typed animation: produces a at a given progress () and writes it through . reverts the target. Concrete subclasses (Double/Color/Point) implement and apply their own easing inside it. The target is either plus , which bind the delegates when the animation begins, or delegates set in code. As in WinUI, a run with no From starts at the value the target shows when it begins — including the value of an animation it takes over from.
- **SUIsei.Animation.BackEase**: Back easing: overshoots slightly before settling. f(t) = t³ − t·A·sin(πt), where A scales the overshoot.
- **SUIsei.Animation.ColorAnimation**: Animates an from to over the duration. Interpolation is component-wise in the authored colour space (a cheap, deterministic lerp).
- **SUIsei.Animation.CubicEase**: Cubic easing: f(t) = t³.
- **SUIsei.Animation.DiscreteValueAnimation`1**: Holds a property at one value while its storyboard runs, as a WinUI ObjectAnimationUsingKeyFrames with a single key at time 0 does: the built-in templates' visual states use it to show a state's brush. It writes the animation rung, so leaving the state releases it and the property shows its own value again. Code-only.
- **SUIsei.Animation.DoubleAnimation**: Animates a scalar from to (or by ) over the duration. A null starts at the target's value when the animation begins; a null with a ends at From + By. Drives a float or double property.
- **SUIsei.Animation.DoubleAnimationUsingKeyFrames**: Animates a scalar through a sequence of s. Each key's is normalized against the ; the value before the first key holds at its value, the value after the last key holds at its value, and each segment is lerped with the upper key's own easing. Keyframes are assumed to be in ascending order.
- **SUIsei.Animation.DoubleBinding**: Binds a double animation to its target. Double animations author in double, as WinUI's do, while SUIsei's own properties are float, so a double animation drives either, converting on write and read.
- **SUIsei.Animation.DoubleKeyFrame**: One key of a : the scalar the animation reaches at (measured from the start of the animation), with an optional shaping the segment that ends at this key.
- **SUIsei.Animation.EasingFunctionBase**: The base of the built-in easing functions. A subclass defines the raw ease-in shape in ; this base mirrors it for and splices the two halves for , matching WinUI.
- **SUIsei.Animation.EasingMode**: Which end of an easing function is shaped.
- **SUIsei.Animation.FillBehavior**: What an animation does to its target when it finishes.
- **SUIsei.Animation.IAnimationTarget**: Something an animation drives on an object: an animatable dependency property, or one of the element channels that animate a property which is not a dependency property. Resolved once when an animation begins.
- **SUIsei.Animation.IAnimationTarget`1**: An of value type : read, write and release, unboxed.
- **SUIsei.Animation.IEasingFunction**: Maps linear progress t in [0,1] to an eased progress.
- **SUIsei.Animation.Lerp`1**: Interpolates from to : 0 gives , 1 gives , and an easing may push it outside that range. A dependency property with one is animatable ().
- **SUIsei.Animation.Lerps**: The standard linear interpolations. A dependency property of one of these types is animatable without declaring a , and tweens them without one.
- **SUIsei.Animation.PointAnimation**: Animates a from to over the duration.
- **SUIsei.Animation.PropertyPath**: What a storyboard animation drives on its target: a dependency property of the target, or one reached through properties whose values are objects, as in WinUI's (UIElement.RenderTransform).(CompositeTransform.TranslateX) or (Border.Background).(SolidColorBrush.Color). The XAML generator resolves a Storyboard.TargetProperty path to one of these at compile time; the steps are walked when the animation begins, and a step may name a more derived type than the property before it holds (a SolidColorBrush property of a Brush), as long as the object found is one.
- **SUIsei.Animation.QuadraticEase**: Quadratic easing: f(t) = t².
- **SUIsei.Animation.RepeatBehavior**: How many times a repeats: a finite iteration or . The default (default(RepeatBehavior)) is a single iteration.
- **SUIsei.Animation.Storyboard**: A group of timelines begun and stopped as a unit — the thing runs and swaps per state. Children are the per-property s; the clock advances each by the storyboard's elapsed time.
- **SUIsei.Animation.Timeline**: The base of everything an advances: a span of animated time with a , a offset, repeat/reverse behaviour, and a fill rule for what happens when it ends. Plain authoring data — the clock owns the running state.
- **SUIsei.Animation.VisualState**: One named look a control can be in — e.g. Normal, PointerOver, Pressed. Entering the state runs its (a null storyboard is the resting/default look).
- **SUIsei.Animation.VisualStateGroup**: A set of mutually exclusive s — e.g. the CommonStates group (Normal/PointerOver/Pressed). Exactly one state in a group is current at a time; entering a new one stops the previous state's storyboard. Groups are independent of one another.
- **SUIsei.Animation.VisualStateManager**: Drives a control between named visual states. The attached property carries the groups on a control's template root; stops the current state's storyboard and starts the target's. When the control is attached to a host its animates the transition; when detached (or useTransitions is false) the target state's end values are applied synchronously so headless tests still observe the result.
- **SUIsei.BrushTransition**: Animates an element's background from one brush to the next when its Background changes, as WinUI's BrushTransition: set it as a Border's, Panel's or ContentPresenter's BackgroundTransition. A change from one to another animates, its colour (opacity included) interpolating over on the host's animation clock; so, as a SUIsei extension, does a change between a solid colour and no brush, which fades the colour in or out. Any other change, and any change while the element is not in a live tree, shows at once. A change that arrives mid-transition starts the next one from the colour on screen.
- **SUIsei.CompositionBrush**: Paint for composition content: what fills a or its border, or colours a . Named after WinUI's composition brushes: a solid colour (), a linear gradient () or an image (). The compositor switches on the concrete type, with no reflection. Paint is retained and mutable, as content is, and versioned on its own: moves on every change to what the brush paints, while the content that holds it keeps its version. One brush may paint many contents: every element showing the same XAML brush shares that brush's one composition brush, so a recolour is one in-place write however many elements show it, and a compositor that keys work on what a content draws reads both versions.
- **SUIsei.CompositionColorBrush**: Paints one colour, as WinUI's CompositionColorBrush.
- **SUIsei.CompositionColorGradientStop**: One colour of a , at along the gradient (0 at its start, 1 at its end).
- **SUIsei.CompositionColorSpace**: The space a gradient interpolates its colours in, as WinUI's CompositionColorSpace (its RGB members).
- **SUIsei.CompositionGradientBrush**: The colour stops and modes a gradient shares, as WinUI's CompositionGradientBrush; a places them along a line. Stops are kept ordered by offset, and two stops at one offset make a hard edge between their colours. Colours interpolate as premultiplied values, the way a GPU interpolates vertex colours. In that is linear light, which a compositor reproduces exactly by splitting the painted geometry where the stops fall and colouring the pieces' corners, with no ramp texture to clamp or quantize colours above paper white. In the interpolation is in the authored, sRGB-encoded values, which are not linear in the light the GPU blends, so each stop interval is cut into pieces sampled exactly at their ends. Between those ends the colour is the straight line in linear light wherever it is sampled, so polygons that share a point, such as the triangles of a shape, agree on its colour.
- **SUIsei.CompositionGradientExtendMode**: What a gradient paints before its start and past its end, as WinUI's CompositionGradientExtendMode.
- **SUIsei.CompositionLinearGradientBrush**: Paints a gradient along the line from to , as WinUI's CompositionLinearGradientBrush: the colour is constant across the line, and stop offsets measure along it.
- **SUIsei.CompositionMappingMode**: What a gradient's points are measured in, as WinUI's CompositionMappingMode.
- **SUIsei.CompositionPath**: A retained, versioned vector path: figures of lines and quadratic and cubic Béziers, with a fill rule. It is the neutral form a geometry takes in the composition layer, named after WinUI's CompositionPath: what the public tessellator reads, and what a foreign compositor renders natively. Elliptical arcs are stored as cubic Béziers of at most 45° each, whose distance from the true ellipse is under 0.0005% of its radius. It is mutable and retained like the rest of the composition content: rebuilding it with and the drawing calls reuses its storage, so a path that keeps its size stops allocating. Every change advances , which work derived from the path (a tessellation) is keyed by.
- **SUIsei.CompositionStrokeStyle**: How a path is stroked: thickness, joins, caps and dashes, as WinUI's composition shapes describe it (CompositionSpriteShape.StrokeThickness, StrokeLineJoin, StrokeMiterLimit, StrokeStartCap, StrokeEndCap, StrokeDashCap, StrokeDashOffset and StrokeDashArray), with the defaults of XAML's Shape. Dash lengths and the dash offset are in multiples of , as in WinUI. Retained and versioned like : every change advances , which a tessellation is keyed by, and setting a value equal to the current one changes nothing.
- **SUIsei.CompositionSurfaceBrush**: Paints an image, as WinUI's CompositionSurfaceBrush: is scaled into the box painted by and placed by the alignment ratios. Only the box is painted: an image that overhangs it is cut at its edges, and one that does not fill it leaves the rest transparent.
- **SUIsei.ContainerVisual**: A grouping node with no content of its own.
- **SUIsei.ContentPropertyAttribute**: Declares which property of a control receives child elements authored without an explicit property-element wrapper in XAML — the WinUI [ContentProperty(Name = "…")]. Read by SUIsei.SourceGen: a single child is assigned to a scalar content property, multiple children are appended to a collection one. Inherited by derived controls unless re-declared.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Border**: A single-child decorator with a background, a border, padding, and rounded corners: measure deflates by border + padding around the child; arrange insets the child by the same; the visual draws a (rounded) fill + border. is treated as uniform for the drawn stroke, and must be uniform.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Button**: A clickable with a default look: a rounded hosting a ({TemplateBinding Content}). As WinUI's default template, the border paints the button's , and , and the presenter its ; where those are unset it shows the built-in look. A CommonStates group shows the pointer-over and pressed backgrounds, faded in and out by the border's . Click synthesis, , and all come from the base.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ButtonBase**: The clickable-control base: the bubbling routed event synthesized from a pointer press+release over the control (or Enter/Space when focused), the common pointer visual states (Normal/PointerOver/Pressed), and WinUI / support. A concrete button supplies its look via a ; is the single override point (e.g. a toggle).
- **SUIsei.Controls.Canvas**: Absolute positioning by the attached /: children measure unconstrained and arrange at their (Left, Top) with their desired size; the Canvas itself desires nothing.
- **SUIsei.Controls.CheckBox**: A with a check-box look: a square box hosting an inner fill glyph, beside a label. The glyph is hidden when unchecked, the accent fill when checked, and a dimmer fill when indeterminate, and the box border picks up the accent while (in)determinate. The box itself reacts to the pointer through a CommonStates group (hover lightens it, press darkens it). As in WinUI's default template, the row behind box and label paints the check box's , and the label its ; the box keeps its own look. (A drawn check mark awaits a glyph in the font atlas; the filled box is the representation used.)
- **SUIsei.Controls.ContentControl**: Hosts a single . Without a it hosts the content directly (a as-is; a string wrapped in a , which colours) and paints behind it. With a template, the control's visual tree comes from the template and a {TemplateBinding Content} routes into the template's ; lets that binding stay live.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ContentHelper**: Shared content-hosting policy: a is hosted as-is; a string (or any other object) is wrapped in a . Used by both and so the rule lives in one place.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ContentPresenter**: Presents a single — the lightweight presenter a control template points at. When a is set, the content is realized through that ; otherwise a is hosted as-is and any other value is wrapped in a (the shared policy), which colours. An optional lets it stand in for a panel.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Control**: The base of templatable controls. Sets to true by default so all controls participate in Tab navigation. A defines the visual tree: it is applied lazily on first measure, becomes the control's single visual child, and carries the groups.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ControlTemplate**: Defines a control's visual tree. The — generated from a <ControlTemplate>, or hand-written — news the subtree given the templated control, wiring its {TemplateBinding}s and groups at instantiation.
- **SUIsei.Controls.DataTemplate**: Defines the visual tree for a data item — used by and items controls to realize one subtree per item. The news the subtree given the item and wires its template-scoped {x:Bind}s against the item.
- **SUIsei.Controls.FrameworkTemplate**: The base of the compile-time templates. A template is a generated factory that news a subtree — never reflection — so and differ only in what the factory is handed (the templated control vs the data item).
- **SUIsei.Controls.Grid**: A row/column grid: Pixel tracks are fixed, Auto tracks size to their largest child, and Star tracks share the leftover space by weight after Pixel/Auto are subtracted. Children select a cell with the attached / and may span tracks with /. An empty definition list defaults to one Star track. Limitation: a spanning child does not drive Auto-track sizing (only single-cell children do).
- **SUIsei.Controls.IItemContainerSource**: The contract a virtualizing panel pulls item containers from — implemented by . The panel realizes only the containers in its viewport and recycles the rest, so a large list never materializes all its containers at once.
- **SUIsei.Controls.IVirtualizingItemsHost**: A panel that virtualizes its children by pulling them from an . An detects this on its panel and hands it the source instead of pushing all the containers itself.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Image**: Draws an , scaled into its layout bounds per and cut at them. Measures to the source's natural pixel size (in DIPs) so an unconstrained image takes its intrinsic size; an explicit Width/Height on the element overrides that as usual. Its content is a rectangle filled by a , centred, except that keeps the image at the top left.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ItemsControl**: Lays out one container per item of in an . Each container is realized through (a ) or, with no template, by wrapping the item. When the source implements the realized containers are updated incrementally (add/remove/replace/move/reset) rather than rebuilt.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ItemsPanelTemplate**: Builds the an lays its item containers out in. The default is a vertical ; a virtualizing list supplies a instead.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ListView**: An that wraps each item in a selectable . Clicking an item selects it (driving the item's SelectionStates visual); single selection is supported (full multi-select is a later refinement).
- **SUIsei.Controls.ListViewItem**: The container a wraps each item in. A SelectionStates group shows a selection highlight behind the content, holding the item's background at the selection brush while it is selected, faded in and out; the owning list calls when the selection changes. Unselected, the item paints its own .
- **SUIsei.Controls.MenuBar**: A horizontal bar of s — the classic application menu (File, Edit, …). Items lay out left to right over a solid bar ; the bar keeps at most one item's drop-down open at a time, closing the previous one when another opens.
- **SUIsei.Controls.MenuBarItem**: A top-level entry in a : a showing a that, when invoked, opens its as a anchored below it. The flat template highlights on hover/press through a CommonStates group, and, as WinUI's default template, paints the item's , and , and its label in ; the owning keeps at most one item's menu open at a time.
- **SUIsei.Controls.MenuFlyout**: A context menu: opens a list of in the root's overlay layer just below the target, with a full-surface light-dismiss layer behind it. Invoking an item (which fires its / ) or pressing outside closes it.
- **SUIsei.Controls.MenuFlyoutItem**: A single command row in a : a with a label and a flat full-width template that highlights on hover. As in WinUI's default template, the row paints the item's , and , and the label its . Click invocation and come from the base; the flyout closes itself on invoke.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Panel**: The base of multi-child layout containers: owns the collection and an optional . Subclasses implement the measure/arrange policy.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Popup**: A transient overlay: when is set, its is composited above the root's content at (, ) and hit-tested on top. The popup element itself occupies no layout space. With a full-surface layer behind the child closes the popup on an outside press. The popup must be attached to a live root (in the element tree) for to take effect; drives the overlay imperatively.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ScrollViewer**: A clipping viewport over a single oversized . Measures the content unbounded in the scroll axis to learn its extent, arranges it offset by the scroll position, and clips to the viewport. Scrolls by mouse wheel, by keyboard (Page/Home/End/arrows when a descendant is focused), and programmatically; the offset is always clamped to /. Pairs with , which reports its full extent for exactly this viewport.
- **SUIsei.Controls.SelectionMode**: How many items a allows selected at once.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Slider**: A range control that picks a in [, ] by dragging a thumb along a track, clicking the track, or with the keyboard. The default template draws an unfilled rail, an accent fill up to the thumb, and a draggable thumb, and carries a CommonStates visual-state group (Normal/PointerOver/Pressed/Disabled) that the pointer drives. is coerced into range and snapped to on input; lets a {x:Bind Value, Mode=TwoWay} push edits back to a view model.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Slider.SliderTrack**: The slider's visual: it lays out the rail (full length), the accent fill (up to the thumb), and the thumb (at the value's fraction of the usable travel) directly from the owning , so the geometry is recomputed on every arrange with no relayout feedback.
- **SUIsei.Controls.StackPanel**: Stacks children end-to-end along : the stacking axis is measured unconstrained (∞), desired = sum along it and max across it; arrange lays children out one after another, each stretched on the cross axis.
- **SUIsei.Controls.TemplateStates**: What the built-in templates' visual states are made of. As in WinUI's default templates, a state shows a brush of its own (a pointer-over or pressed background) by holding the part's Background at it while the state is current, and the resting state hands the background back to what the template bound it to, usually the control's own . The part's fades between them. The hand-back is a storyboard of its own rather than WinUI's empty state: the clock lets a storyboard go once it has finished, holding its end value, so leaving the state that holds a brush cannot release it. The resting state's storyboard clears the held value instead, on the clock's next step.
- **SUIsei.Controls.TextBlock**: A run of text. Measures and emits glyphs against the engine's default MTSDF font (): an advance-based width (no HarfBuzz shaping) and a the compositor lays out into draws.
- **SUIsei.Controls.TextBox**: A single-line editable text field. Consumes the host's and events (the input pipeline already routes them to the focused element) to drive a caret + selection over : insert/overtype, Backspace/Delete, arrow/Home/End motion (Shift extends the selection), Select-All, and cut/copy/paste through a process-wide clipboard (an OS clipboard is a later host seam). is a dependency property with a event, so it participates in TwoWay {x:Bind}. IME is deferred — committed characters only.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ToggleButton**: A that holds a checked state — the base for . A click cycles (two-state, or three-state through null when is set), raising // and driving the CheckStates visual-state group. Subclasses reflect the state in template parts via .
- **SUIsei.Controls.UIElementCollection**: The ordered child collection of a ; adds re-parent the child and invalidate the owner's measure.
- **SUIsei.Controls.VirtualizingStackPanel**: A vertical items panel that realizes only the containers intersecting its viewport. It assumes one uniform row height (, suisei:Virtualization.RowHeight in XAML), so the visible window is pure arithmetic from ; containers that scroll out are recycled back to the . It reports the full extent (ItemCount × row height) so an outer scroller sees the true size. It has no variable-height virtualization, scroll chrome, or wheel and scrollbar input: the offset is set directly.
- **SUIsei.CornerRadius**: The radii of a rectangle's four corners in DIPs, as WinUI's CornerRadius. SUIsei draws one radius for all four corners, so an element given radii that differ throws rather than drawing something else.
- **SUIsei.DependencyObject**: The base of everything that carries dependency properties. Holds a sparse, int-keyed effective-value store and resolves the WinUI value-precedence ladder: Animation > Local > Style > Inherited > Default A set recomputes the top of the ladder, coerces it, fires the typed change callback only when the coerced resolved value changes, and ORs the property's into the element (via ). Reflection-free: dispatch goes through the typed delegates on . The store is typed: each property's rungs live in a slot of the property's own value type, made on the first write of that property to this object. After that a write, its coercion, its change check and its change callback never box, so animating a value-type property every frame allocates nothing.
- **SUIsei.DependencyObject.ValueRung**: A rung of the precedence ladder below the default, highest first.
- **SUIsei.DependencyProperty**: A reflection-free dependency property — the WinUI semantics (typed metadata, change/coerce callbacks, value precedence) with the -keyed, string-dispatched mechanism replaced by a dense integer slot () and typed delegates. Abstract base; the concrete property is always a . Identity is by reference.
- **SUIsei.DependencyPropertyChangedEventArgs**: The data for a dependency-property change event such as : the property and its old and new values, as in WinUI.
- **SUIsei.DependencyPropertyChangedEventHandler**: Handles a dependency-property change event.
- **SUIsei.DependencyPropertyKind**: Whether a property is declared on its owner () or attached to arbitrary targets (, e.g. Grid.Row). Both share the one dense index space.
- **SUIsei.DependencyProperty`2**: The concrete, typed dependency property.
- **SUIsei.DrawListBuffers**: One set of a surface's retained draw-list streams. A keeps two and fills them in turn, so the list it built last stays readable while it builds the next. names the composite that last filled the set; a bound to an older revision has had its contents overwritten.
- **SUIsei.DrawListCompositor**: Loom's default : walks a surface's composition tree, folds transform/clip/opacity into a pre-transformed vertex/command stream, and exposes it as a neutral . Emits the rectangle family (fills + borders), MSDF glyph runs and vector shapes (, through the prim), painted by colour, linear-gradient or image brushes; a gradient is drawn exactly by cutting the geometry where its colour stops being linear (). Output is asserted on CPU via — the primary test seam, no backend needed.
- **SUIsei.DrawListCompositor.RectShapes**: The outlines of a rect's rounded fill and of its border ring (the rect less its inner rounded rect, whose radius is the corner radius less the thickness, as the rect prims draw it), for the rects an image paints. Kept on the content as its derived work, with their tessellations, and rebuilt only when the size, radius or thickness change.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.AtlasImage**: A glyph atlas page: the decoded RGBA8 MTSDF texels exposes. SUIsei decodes the atlas PNG itself (no engine dependency); as a the page reaches the host through the slot table of every draw list whose glyph runs sample it. The texels are signed distances, never sRGB.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.DrawCommand**: One batched draw call in a draw list: a contiguous slice of the index stream drawn under a scissor rectangle with one texture bound. Blittable and sequentially laid out — the engine glue can reinterpret its memory as the equivalent engine draw command without copying.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.DrawListBuilder**: Builds a by hand, with the draw list the compositor uses: vector geometry from the , and group layers. It is the public way from tessellated paths to vertices and commands, for a foreign that wants SUIsei's draw contract, a host's own overlays, and tests. Like a compositor's surface, a builder keeps two sets of buffers and fills them in turn: the list one returns stays readable through the next build, its streams throw once the build after that reuses them, and building lists of a steady size allocates nothing.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.DrawListData**: One frame's flattened draw list — a variable-size vertex stream, its 16-bit index stream, and the batched draw commands that scissor + texture + index-range it. Backend-neutral (no graphics-API types), so the whole producer pipeline up to GPU upload is CPU-testable against . Rebuilt only when its source changes; an unchanged frame re-submits the same Revision. A list a produced is a view over buffers the compositor keeps and refills. It stays readable through the next composite of its surface, which fills a second set of buffers, and its streams (, , , , ) throw once a later composite refills its own set. Memory and spans taken from it share that lifetime but are not checked. The compositor also reuses the view objects, so a reference kept for four or more composites can be rebound to a newer list: read the surface's current list each frame rather than keeping one.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.DrawListId**: Identifies one draw list a surface's compositor produces each frame.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.EarClipper**: Triangulates a simple polygon with holes by ear clipping, after the algorithm of mapbox's earcut (ISC licence, © Mapbox): each hole is bridged into the outer ring at a vertex visible from its leftmost point, then ears (convex vertices whose triangle holds no other vertex) are clipped until one triangle is left. Degenerate input falls back to removing collinear points, curing local self-crossings and splitting along a valid diagonal, so it always terminates. The outer ring has a positive signed area (Σ x_i y_(i+1) - x_(i+1) y_i) and every hole a negative one. Nodes live in a retained pool, so triangulating polygons of a steady size allocates nothing.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.IVectorSink**: Receives the triangles a draws when emitted: the draw list's vector emitter, or a foreign compositor's own buffer. Implemented by a struct, it is called with no virtual dispatch and no allocation.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.ImageSource**: A decoded RGBA8 image an draws. SUIsei stays GPU-free: the source holds neutral pixels (decoded with StbImageSharp, the same decoder as ), and as a it reaches the host through the slot table of every draw list that draws it; the host uploads it once and binds it by slot.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.OverlayVertex**: The vertex of a 2D overlay draw list — a pixel-space position, texture coordinate, premultiplied colour, and a float4 of per-vertex data the consuming technique defines. Blittable and sequentially laid out so it can be uploaded directly to a GPU vertex buffer.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.PremultipliedHdrColor**: A premultiplied RGBA16F colour — the wire format for the overlay vertex stream. Four Half components (8 bytes), blittable and sequentially laid out so the engine can upload it directly as GPU vertex data. Named PremultipliedHdrColor (not a bare four-Half vector) so the premultiplied-alpha contract is explicit in the type system; produced by .
- **SUIsei.Drawing.StrokePrimitives**: The triangles a stroke is built from, each carrying the signed distances to the edges it antialiases. Shared by the tessellator, which builds a whole stroke, and by trimming at emit, which rebuilds the pieces cut at the trim points, so both draw identical geometry. Every piece reaches margin (half a pixel) past the true outline, so the antialiasing ramp is rasterized on the outside, and every distance is linear across its triangle. A triangle carries only the edges whose ramps it holds: a segment's body its two sides and any cap clip, a join or cap one outer edge per triangle (joins and caps are split on their bisectors so two nearly parallel edges never share a triangle, where the product of their ramps would darken the edge).
- **SUIsei.Drawing.SweepTessellator**: The GLU sweep-line tessellator (Eric Veach, SGI), ported from libtess2 under SGI Free Software License B: it resolves contours that cross themselves and each other into the planar arrangement they describe, keeps the regions a winding rule calls inside, and either triangulates them or returns their boundary as simple contours. Robust to degenerate input: coincident vertices merge, crossings get vertices, and zero-length edges and two-edge faces go. Planar only: the sweep plane is the input's own (s = x, t = y), with no normal to compute. The mesh, the event queue and the edge dictionary are pooled and their storage retained, so tessellating inputs of a steady size allocates nothing once warm.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.SweepTessellator.ActiveRegion**: The region between a pair of adjacent edges crossing the sweep line. Regions are kept in order in the edge dictionary; as the sweep line crosses each vertex, the affected regions are updated.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.SweepTessellator.DictNode**: A node of the edge dictionary: a sorted, circular, doubly-linked list with a key-less head.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.SweepTessellator.PriorityQueue**: The sweep's event queue: the vertices in VertLeq order, with insertion of new (intersection) vertices and deletion by handle. The initial vertices are sorted once into an array consumed from its end; vertices inserted later go into a heap. Extraction takes the smaller of the two minimums. Handles below zero name sorted-array slots, others heap handles. Its arrays are retained and grow by doubling.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.TessellatedPath**: A tessellated fill or stroke: triangles with three vertices each, never shared, whose corners carry the distances the vector prim antialiases with and their arc length. It is retained: tessellating into it again reuses its storage, so a path that keeps its size stops allocating, and drawing it, moved, recoloured or trimmed, allocates nothing. A stroke keeps its triangles in pieces ordered along its length: caps, segment bodies and joins. draws a trimmed stroke from those pieces: the ones inside the trim as they are, the two segments it cuts rebuilt to the trim points, and new caps there, so a draw-on animation never re-tessellates.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.TessellatedPath.Emitter`1**: Copies cached pieces to the sink, coalescing neighbours into one call, and rebuilds cut pieces into retained scratch.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.TessellatedPath.Piece**: One piece of a stroke: its run-coordinate range (a single point for a join or cap), its vertices, and for a body its segment, where along the segment it starts, and whether it carries its run's flat or square cap clip.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.TessellatedPath.Run**: One continuous stretch of stroke: a whole open figure, a whole closed figure (a loop), or one dash. Its range is in run coordinates, the figure's arc length, which runs past the figure's length when a dash crosses a closed figure's start.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.TessellatedPath.Segment**: One straight segment of a flattened figure: where it starts, its unit direction, its length, and the figure-local arc length at its start.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.TessellationScale**: The pixel scale a path is tessellated for, rounded to buckets half an octave wide, so a path that scales a little keeps its tessellation and one that zooms a lot gets a new one. Curves are flattened to within a quarter pixel at the top of the bucket of the largest scale the transform applies; antialiasing reaches half a pixel past each edge at the bottom of the bucket of the smallest, so it is never narrower than a pixel however the bucket rounds.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.Tessellator**: Turns a into antialiased triangles for the vector prim: a fill, or a stroke with WinUI's joins, caps and dashes. Curves are flattened to within a quarter pixel at the ; every edge the result shows carries a signed distance, so a renderer antialiases it exactly at any position, rotation or scale within the bucket. Public and dependency-free, so a foreign compositor can tessellate the composition's paths itself. It keeps scratch buffers between calls and writes into a retained , so re-tessellating paths of a steady size allocates nothing. One tessellator is not safe to use from two threads at once.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.Tessellator.Contour**: One contour to fill: a range of , its signed area, and what the nesting analysis decided about it.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.Tessellator.FigureRuns**: Where a figure's segments are in the output, and its length and offset along the whole geometry.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.Tessellator.FlatFigure**: One flattened figure: a range of , whether it is closed, whether it is filled, and whether it draws at all (a lone move does not).
- **SUIsei.Drawing.TextureSource**: Texels a draw list samples through one of its texture slots: an , a glyph atlas page (), or the texel. A host uploads each source it meets in a list's and binds it by slot. A source is identified by reference, and moves when its texels change, so a host replaces an upload only when it is out of date.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.VectorVertex**: One corner of a tessellated triangle: its position in the path's local space, the four signed distances a renderer turns into antialiased coverage, and its arc length along the stroke.
- **SUIsei.Extensions.Clipping**: Clipping to an element's own bounds, set in XAML as suisei:Clipping.ClipToBounds="True". WinUI has no such property: it clips with UIElement.Clip, a geometry. Here the element's composition node clips its subtree to the element's layout bounds. Controls that always clip (ScrollViewer, TextBox) do so whatever this says.
- **SUIsei.Extensions.Scrolling**: Scrolling settings WinUI has no property for, set on a in XAML as suisei:Scrolling.WheelScrollAmount="64".
- **SUIsei.Extensions.StrokeBrushMapping**: How a shape's stroke gradient is mapped, set in XAML as suisei:StrokeBrushMapping.Mode="AlongLength": with the gradient's offsets run along the stroke's untrimmed length, for a fade along a trail or a line coloured by progress. WinUI has no such mapping; it is set on the shape rather than the brush, so a brush shared by several elements never changes meaning with who shows it. It is exact: the stroke is cut where its colour stops being linear along it (at each stop), so a stop's colour lands exactly at its offset along the length. It suits a few stops; colouring each sample of a long line differently is a different feature, not provided. A solid or image stroke draws as usual.
- **SUIsei.Extensions.StrokeBrushMappingMode**: How a shape's Stroke gradient is laid over the stroke, set by .
- **SUIsei.Extensions.StrokeTrim**: The part of a shape's stroke that is drawn, set in XAML as suisei:StrokeTrim.End="0.5": WinUI's CompositionGeometry.TrimStart, TrimEnd and TrimOffset lifted into markup, for draw-on reveals and segments that run round an outline. The values are fractions of the whole outline's length, all its figures in order: the stroke runs from Start to End, both moved along by Offset and wrapping past the end back to the start. Start and end are clamped to 0..1 and swapped when start is the larger; equal, they draw nothing. The trim applies where the shape is drawn: animating it, through a path such as (suisei:StrokeTrim.End), costs no layout and no tessellation, and allocates nothing. A trimmed stroke takes its start cap where it starts and its end cap where it ends. The fill is not trimmed.
- **SUIsei.Extensions.Virtualization**: Settings for SUIsei's , set in XAML as <VirtualizingStackPanel suisei:Virtualization.RowHeight="32" /> inside an ItemsPanelTemplate. WinUI's virtualizing panels measure their items; SUIsei's assumes one uniform row height, so the visible window is arithmetic from the scroll offset.
- **SUIsei.FocusManager**: Per-host focus state machine. Tracks the focused element, raises the four focus routed events (GettingFocus/LosingFocus tunnel, GotFocus/LostFocus bubble), and drives Tab/Shift-Tab navigation across a set of s respecting , and . Tab order runs across all the views as one sequence: no subtree keeps focus within itself, and is not read.
- **SUIsei.FocusState**: How focus was most recently acquired on an element (WinUI-compatible).
- **SUIsei.FontAtlas**: A baked MTSDF font atlas: the decoded atlas page plus per-glyph layout, loaded from the pair an MSDF generator emits — a PNG page (RGBA8 MTSDF) and a JSON layout. The page is decoded linear/UNORM, no mips: MTSDF texels are signed distances, never sRGB colour. Plane bounds are EM units in a y-down, baseline-at-origin frame.
- **SUIsei.FrameworkElement**: Adds the WinUI framework-level layout inputs on top of : explicit / (NaN = Auto), / (and the height pair), , and alignment. It implements the WinUI MeasureCore/ArrangeCore wrapper — deflate by margin, clamp to min/max/explicit, call the element's MeasureOverride/ArrangeOverride, reinflate — so every control only writes its intrinsic sizing. Backing storage uses the C# 14 field keyword (no hand-declared fields).
- **SUIsei.Glyph**: One baked glyph from a . Plane bounds are EM units in a y-down, baseline-at-origin frame (the on-screen quad, scaled by the font px size); the UV rect addresses the glyph's MTSDF cell in the atlas page (0..1, v=0 at the top — the atlas is baked with yOrigin: top). Whitespace glyphs set false and carry only an . is the source Unicode code point (−1 for a glyph with none, e.g. a ligature in a glyph-id-keyed atlas). is the font glyph index (−1 in a codepoint-keyed atlas that does not record ids) — the key a shaper such as HarfBuzz addresses glyphs by.
- **SUIsei.GlyphRunContent**: A run of laid-out text drawn from a . The compositor lays the glyphs out against its font through the atlas's shaper, emitting commands. is the on-screen size in surface pixels (DIPs × scale); colours the glyphs, a gradient measured over .
- **SUIsei.GradientLine**: Where a linear gradient lies in the local space of what it paints: measures a point along it, 0 at the start and 1 at the end, constant across it. A gradient whose start and end coincide is , and paints its last stop's colour everywhere.
- **SUIsei.GradientSplitter**: Paints convex polygons with a linear gradient exactly, with no ramp texture: the polygon is cut into bands wherever the gradient's colour stops being linear along it (each stop, each repeat of a wrapping gradient, and each piece of an sRGB-interpolated interval), and every corner of every band gets the gradient's colour at that point. Within a band the colour is linear in position, which is exactly what interpolating vertex colours across a triangle produces, so a GPU and the CPU rasterizer draw the gradient itself, colours above paper white included. Each corner keeps its uv, interpolated where a cut crosses an edge, so a rectangle's bands keep their part of its 0..1 uv (the rounded-rectangle and border shading reads it, with the whole rectangle's size, to find its edges) and a glyph's pieces keep their part of its atlas cell. A vector triangle's pieces keep their part of its edge distances the same way, which are linear across it, so the pieces antialias exactly as the whole triangle would. Allocation-free: the pieces are built on the stack.
- **SUIsei.GridLength**: A Grid row/column track length — fixed pixels, Auto (max child desired), or a * weight of the leftover space (WinUI GridLength). Default is 1*, matching WinUI.
- **SUIsei.GridUnitType**: How a is interpreted: a fixed DIP size, content-sized, or a proportional star.
- **SUIsei.HdrColor**: An authoring colour — float RGBA where 0..1 is SDR / paper-white range and a component >1 is above paper white (opt-in HDR). Named HdrColor (not Color) for explicitness and to dodge the clash. Folded to a by the compositor; the paper-white reference scale is applied in the shader.
- **SUIsei.HorizontalAlignment**: WinUI alignment within a layout slot's horizontal axis. fills the slot.
- **SUIsei.HotReload**: XAML Hot Reload support. A generated view registers itself here in InitializeComponent() and each registers itself on construction. When the runtime applies a metadata delta (an edited .xaml re-runs the source generator under dotnet watch), the records the changed types; the next drains them and rebuilds the affected views on the UI thread — never on the hot-reload agent's thread. Bookkeeping is gated on , which defaults to : it is false under NativeAOT / optimized publish, so the whole mechanism is inert and trimmable there, preserving the reflection-free runtime. Tests force it on.
- **SUIsei.HotReloadHandler**: The [MetadataUpdateHandler] target (registered as an assembly attribute in ). The runtime invokes these after applying a metadata delta; they hand the changed types to , which defers the actual view rebuild to the next .
- **SUIsei.IGlyphSource**: The font read-surface a text shaper (and any glyph consumer) needs, independent of how glyphs are imaged: code-point and glyph-id lookups returning the drawable cell, advances, and EM line metrics. is the MTSDF implementation; a different imagery backend (e.g. a bitmap atlas) can implement the same interface, so the shaping backend () and the imagery backend swap independently — a shaper is written against this interface, never a concrete atlas. Render-technique specifics (e.g. an MTSDF distance range) are deliberately kept off this interface.
- **SUIsei.ISubPropertyListener**: Something that shows a shared sub-property object (a brush, a transform, a gradient stop, a geometry) and is told when that object changes, so it can bring what it draws up to date without re-reading anything else. An element listens to the brushes, transform and clip geometry it shows while it is in a live tree; a brush listens to its gradient stops, a transform group to its children, and a geometry to its figures, segments and points.
- **SUIsei.ITextShaper**: Turns a run of text into positioned glyphs against an — it is written against the source interface, never a concrete atlas, so the shaping backend and the imagery backend stay independent. The default is advance-based, one glyph per code point (no kerning or ligatures); a real shaper (e.g. HarfBuzz) applies the font's GSUB/GPOS to produce ligatures, contextual forms, and kerning, resolving the glyph ids it emits back through the source. A owns the active shaper, so swapping it changes layout everywhere (measure, the compositor's glyph runs, caret math) at once.
- **SUIsei.IUICompositor**: The portability boundary: renders a surface's tree. Loom ships ; a foreign engine substitutes its own and consumes the tree directly.
- **SUIsei.IValueConverter**: Converts a value between binding source and target types. Implement this for converter= attributes in XAML bindings; pass a singleton instance via {StaticResource key}.
- **SUIsei.Input.FocusNavigationDirection**: Direction of programmatic or keyboard-driven focus movement.
- **SUIsei.Input.KeyInput**: One device-neutral keyboard event the host queues into between frames. The host (Sandbox/Silk.NET) translates raw platform key events into this, keeping windowing types out of SUIsei.
- **SUIsei.Input.ModifierKeys**: Modifier keys held at the time of a keyboard or pointer event.
- **SUIsei.Input.PointerButtons**: The set of pointer buttons currently held.
- **SUIsei.Input.PointerDeviceType**: The kind of device that produced a — WinUI-shaped and device-neutral so no host (Silk.NET) type leaks into SUIsei. Only is currently driven; pen and touch use the same struct.
- **SUIsei.Input.PointerInput**: One device-neutral pointer event the host queues into a between frames. WinUI-shaped so mouse, pen and touch share one struct; the host (Sandbox/Silk.NET) translates raw input into this, keeping graphics/windowing types out of SUIsei. is in surface pixels (the same space as the composited DrawListData / the framebuffer); the host hit-tests and routes it in .
- **SUIsei.Input.PointerUpdateKind**: What changed in a — the WinUI PointerUpdateKind. A plain move carries ; a button edge carries the specific pressed/released kind that the input pipeline turns into PointerPressed/PointerReleased routed events (and, on a matching pair, a synthesized Click).
- **SUIsei.Input.VirtualKey**: Virtual key codes (WinUI-compatible subset). Values match Windows virtual-key codes so host adapters can cast directly from platform key enumerations.
- **SUIsei.InputManager**: Per-host pointer routing: hit-tests each queued over the host's interactive overlay views, raises tunnel-then-bubble pointer routed events, tracks the "over" chain (so enter/exit fire per element), implicitly captures on press so a press→release pair routes to the same target (the basis for Button.Click), and supports explicit drag capture via /. Persistent host state; headless (no engine/backend).
- **SUIsei.InvalidationFlags**: Which layout/render stages a property change invalidates — ORed up the tree on a resolved-value change A pure-render change (a brush colour) sets only ; a sizing change sets .
- **SUIsei.LayerEffect**: A composition-tree post effect applied to a group's render-to-texture layer. A visual that carries an effect is always composited as one bitmap (exactly like a sub-1 group opacity), and the effect is applied when the layer is composited back into its parent. selects the effect the backend runs; .. are its parameters. Id 0 is the identity (opacity-only); id 1 is a Gaussian blur whose pixel sigma is .
- **SUIsei.ListenerList**: The s a shared sub-property object tells when it changes. A listener that shows the object twice (an element using one brush for its background and its border) is added, told and removed once per use. Telling them allocates nothing.
- **SUIsei.Markup.IPathMarkupSink**: What reports as it reads WinUI path markup: the fill rule, then each figure as a start point and drawing commands, all in absolute coordinates. Relative commands, H/V and the smooth S/T forms arrive already resolved to the absolute line and curve they draw.
- **SUIsei.Markup.PathMarkup**: WinUI's path markup, the move-and-draw command syntax of Path.Data: an optional fill rule (F0 even-odd, F1 nonzero), then figures, each a move (M) followed by lines (L, H, V), cubic Béziers (C, smooth S), quadratic Béziers (Q, smooth T), elliptical arcs (A) and an optional close (Z). A lowercase command is relative to the current point, and a command's parameters may repeat to draw several of it (after M, further points are lines). Numbers are separated by commas and/or whitespace and must be finite; arc flags are 0 or 1. The grammar is held strictly: markup must start with a move, a close is followed by a move or the end, and anything else is an error naming its character position. This file is compiled into both the runtime and the netstandard2.0 XAML generator, so markup in XAML is checked at compile time by the parser the runtime uses.
- **SUIsei.Markup.XamlValueSyntax**: The text forms XAML values take: colours (#RRGGBB, #AARRGGBB, or one of WinUI's named colours) and lists of numbers separated by commas or whitespace (points, vectors, thicknesses). This file is compiled into both the runtime and the netstandard2.0 XAML generator, which links it as source, so a value the generator accepts at compile time parses the same way at runtime. It uses only APIs both targets have.
- **SUIsei.Media.AlignmentX**: Where a tile brush places its content across the area painted, as WinUI's AlignmentX.
- **SUIsei.Media.AlignmentY**: Where a tile brush places its content down the area painted, as WinUI's AlignmentY.
- **SUIsei.Media.ArcSegment**: An elliptical arc to , as WinUI's ArcSegment: part of an ellipse with radii , rotated by degrees. Of the four arcs such an ellipse can draw between the two points, and pick one. Radii too small to reach the end grow, keeping their ratio, until they just do.
- **SUIsei.Media.BezierSegment**: A cubic Bézier curve to , bent by the control points and , as WinUI's BezierSegment.
- **SUIsei.Media.Brush**: What paints an element's area, text or border, as WinUI's Brush: a , a or an . A brush is shareable, as in WinUI: put one in a ResourceDictionary and give it to many elements. Each brush keeps one retained , which every element showing it paints with, and a change to the brush updates that paint in place and marks those elements' visuals dirty, with no layout and no allocation. An element registers with a brush while it is in a live tree and unregisters when it leaves, so a long-lived brush does not keep removed elements, or the trees a hot-reload rebuild replaced, alive. Because the brush is shared, so are its animations: a storyboard that animates a shared brush, such as (Border.Background).(SolidColorBrush.Color) on a border whose background is a resource, recolours every element showing that brush, as it does in WinUI. Give an element its own brush to animate it alone. Like any dependency object, a brush belongs to the UI thread of the elements that show it. The brushes of SUIsei's built-in control look are the exception: they are sealed, so they are shared by every control on every thread, keep no listeners, and throw if anything tries to change them.
- **SUIsei.Media.BrushMappingMode**: What a gradient brush's points are measured in, as WinUI's BrushMappingMode.
- **SUIsei.Media.ColorInterpolationMode**: The space a gradient's colours interpolate in, as WinUI's ColorInterpolationMode.
- **SUIsei.Media.CompositeTransform**: Scale, skew, rotation and translation in one, as WinUI's CompositeTransform, applied in that order: scale, skew and rotation about (, ), then the translation. Angles are in degrees. The usual target of a storyboard that moves an element: (UIElement.RenderTransform).(CompositeTransform.TranslateX).
- **SUIsei.Media.DoubleCollection**: An ordered list of numbers, as WinUI's DoubleCollection: a shape's dash pattern, for one. Every change is reported to the element using it. In XAML it is written as numbers separated by commas or spaces, StrokeDashArray="2 1".
- **SUIsei.Media.EllipseGeometry**: An axis-aligned ellipse around , as WinUI's EllipseGeometry. A zero radius draws nothing.
- **SUIsei.Media.FillRule**: How a geometry whose figures overlap or cross themselves decides what is inside, as WinUI's FillRule.
- **SUIsei.Media.GeneralTransform**: Maps points and rects from one coordinate space to another, as WinUI's GeneralTransform: the base of every , and what returns. A transform that cannot map a point (one into an element scaled to nothing) reports it through .
- **SUIsei.Media.Geometry**: A 2D shape, as WinUI's Geometry: what a Path draws and what clips to. Every property of every part is a dependency property, so geometries are stylable and their numbers animatable. A change anywhere in a geometry, down to one point of a segment, is reported to its listeners: the group or element using it. An element registers while it is in a live tree and unregisters when it leaves, so a geometry kept in a resource dictionary never keeps removed elements alive. Each geometry keeps its , the neutral path the compositor and the tessellator read, and rebuilds it in place after a change, reusing its storage. A geometry is drawn in the local space of the element that draws it, through its if it has one. The transform is applied where the geometry is used rather than to its path, so moving it does not rebuild the path.
- **SUIsei.Media.GeometryCollection**: A geometry group's children, as WinUI's GeometryCollection. A geometry may be in several collections, and in one more than once.
- **SUIsei.Media.GeometryGroup**: Several geometries drawn as one, as WinUI's GeometryGroup: their figures together, each through its own , filled by the group's own (the children's fill rules are not used), so overlapping children cut holes under and merge under . The group's own transform applies on top, where the group is used.
- **SUIsei.Media.GradientBrush**: The stops and modes a gradient brush shares, as WinUI's GradientBrush; places them along a line. The stops are the brush's XAML content: <LinearGradientBrush><GradientStop Color="Red" Offset="0"/>…</LinearGradientBrush> Colours interpolate as premultiplied values. is drawn exactly, colours above paper white included, by splitting what is painted where the stops fall: there is no ramp texture to clamp or quantize them. The default, , cuts each stop interval into eight pieces, exact at their ends and within the error documents between them, and a stop above 1 in it throws when the brush is drawn.
- **SUIsei.Media.GradientSpreadMethod**: What a gradient paints before its start and past its end, as WinUI's GradientSpreadMethod.
- **SUIsei.Media.GradientStop**: One colour of a , at along it, as WinUI's GradientStop. Both are animatable; a change reaches every brush holding the stop, and from there every element showing the brush, with no layout and no allocation. Name a stop with x:Name to target it from a storyboard.
- **SUIsei.Media.GradientStopCollection**: The stops of one , as WinUI's GradientStopCollection, in any order: the brush orders them by offset. Adding, removing or replacing a stop, or changing one, updates the brush's paint in place. A stop may sit in more than one brush's collection, and a change to it reaches each.
- **SUIsei.Media.ImageBrush**: Paints an image, as WinUI's ImageBrush: scaled into the area painted by and placed by and , cut at the area's edges. It paints a Panel's or Border's background, rounded or not, a Border's border, and a shape's fill or stroke; text is not supported yet, and throws when drawn.
- **SUIsei.Media.LineGeometry**: A straight line from to , as WinUI's LineGeometry. It encloses nothing, so it only draws when stroked.
- **SUIsei.Media.LineSegment**: A straight line to , as WinUI's LineSegment.
- **SUIsei.Media.LinearGradientBrush**: Paints a gradient along the line from to , as WinUI's LinearGradientBrush: the colour is constant across the line, and the stops' offsets measure along it. The default line runs from the top left (0,0) to the bottom right (1,1) of the area painted. With that area is the element's: a border's rectangle, or a text block's layout box for its text. If the start and end coincide, the last stop's colour fills the area.
- **SUIsei.Media.MatrixTransform**: An arbitrary affine transform given as a matrix, as WinUI's MatrixTransform. SUIsei's matrix is (single precision, row vectors: M11 M12 / M21 M22 / M31 M32 as WinUI's M11 M12 / M21 M22 / OffsetX OffsetY); in XAML it is six numbers in that order. Not animatable, as a matrix has no interpolation.
- **SUIsei.Media.PathFigure**: One connected outline of a , as WinUI's PathFigure: it starts at and runs through its in order. A figure belongs to one geometry's at a time.
- **SUIsei.Media.PathFigureCollection**: A path geometry's figures, as WinUI's PathFigureCollection. A figure belongs to one collection at a time: adding one that another collection holds throws, as WinUI does.
- **SUIsei.Media.PathGeometry**: A geometry of any shape, as WinUI's PathGeometry: of lines, Béziers and arcs, filled by . In XAML it is written as figure elements, or as path markup where a property takes a (Data="M 0,0 L 10,0 10,10 Z"), which also reads.
- **SUIsei.Media.PathMarkupBuilder**: Builds a from parsed path markup: one figure per move, and one segment per run of the same command, so L 1,1 2,2 3,3 becomes a single and one line stays a . Arcs are one each, as they cannot share one.
- **SUIsei.Media.PathSegment**: One piece of a 's outline, drawn from where the piece before it ended, as WinUI's PathSegment. A segment belongs to one figure's at a time.
- **SUIsei.Media.PathSegmentCollection**: A figure's segments, in drawing order, as WinUI's PathSegmentCollection. A segment belongs to one collection at a time: adding one that another collection holds throws, as WinUI does.
- **SUIsei.Media.PenLineCap**: The shape at the end of a stroke or of one of its dashes, as WinUI's PenLineCap.
- **SUIsei.Media.PenLineJoin**: How a stroke turns a corner, as WinUI's PenLineJoin.
- **SUIsei.Media.PointCollection**: An ordered list of points, as WinUI's PointCollection: the vertices of a poly segment (and of a polyline or polygon). Every change is reported to the geometry or element using it. In XAML it is written as pairs of numbers, Points="0,0 10,10 20,0".
- **SUIsei.Media.PolyBezierSegment**: Cubic Bézier curves, one per three of (two control points and an end point), as WinUI's PolyBezierSegment. Points left over after the last whole three draw nothing.
- **SUIsei.Media.PolyLineSegment**: Straight lines through each of in turn, as WinUI's PolyLineSegment.
- **SUIsei.Media.PolyQuadraticBezierSegment**: Quadratic Bézier curves, one per two of (a control point and an end point), as WinUI's PolyQuadraticBezierSegment. A point left over after the last whole pair draws nothing.
- **SUIsei.Media.QuadraticBezierSegment**: A quadratic Bézier curve to , bent by the control point , as WinUI's QuadraticBezierSegment.
- **SUIsei.Media.RectangleGeometry**: An axis-aligned rectangle, as WinUI's RectangleGeometry: what takes. In XAML, Rect="x,y,width,height".
- **SUIsei.Media.RotateTransform**: Rotates by degrees, clockwise on screen, about (, ), as WinUI's RotateTransform.
- **SUIsei.Media.ScaleTransform**: Scales by and about (, ), as WinUI's ScaleTransform.
- **SUIsei.Media.SkewTransform**: Skews about (, ), as WinUI's SkewTransform: x moves by y·tan() and y by x·tan(), angles in degrees.
- **SUIsei.Media.SolidColorBrush**: Paints one colour, as WinUI's SolidColorBrush. In XAML a colour string (Background="#22252E", Background="CornflowerBlue") makes one.
- **SUIsei.Media.SweepDirection**: The direction an elliptical arc is drawn in, as WinUI's SweepDirection. Directions are as seen on screen, where y grows downward.
- **SUIsei.Media.TileBrush**: A brush that paints content scaled into the area painted, as WinUI's TileBrush: the base of .
- **SUIsei.Media.Transform**: A 2D affine transform, as WinUI's Transform: an element's , or a child of a . Its properties are dependency properties, so a storyboard animates them through paths such as (UIElement.RenderTransform).(CompositeTransform.TranslateX). A change moves every element showing the transform on the visual path, with no layout. Like a brush, a transform may be shared: an element registers with it while it is in a live tree.
- **SUIsei.Media.TransformCollection**: The children of a , as WinUI's TransformCollection. Adding, removing or replacing a child, or changing one, moves every element showing the group.
- **SUIsei.Media.TransformGroup**: Transforms applied one after another, in the order lists them, as WinUI's TransformGroup. A change to any child, or to the list, moves every element showing the group.
- **SUIsei.Media.TranslateTransform**: Moves by (, ) DIPs, as WinUI's TranslateTransform.
- **SUIsei.Orientation**: The axis a stacks along.
- **SUIsei.PathFigureInfo**: Where one figure of a lies in its and , starting with its .
- **SUIsei.PathTrim**: The part of a path's stroke that is drawn, as WinUI's CompositionGeometry.TrimStart, TrimEnd and TrimOffset: fractions of the whole geometry's length, all its figures in order. The stroke runs from to , both moved by and wrapping past the end of the path back to its start, so animating runs a fixed-length piece round a path. Start and end are clamped to 0..1 and swapped when start is the larger; equal, they draw nothing. A trimmed stroke takes its start cap where it starts and its end cap where it ends. Trimming changes which part of a tessellated stroke is drawn, not the tessellation, so animating a trim never re-tessellates. It applies to strokes; a fill is not trimmed.
- **SUIsei.PathVerb**: One drawing command of a , with the number of points it takes from .
- **SUIsei.Point**: A point in DIPs (layout-space). Distinct from only for readability at call sites.
- **SUIsei.PropertyMetadata`2**: The typed metadata for a : default value, a typed change callback (old, new — no boxing on the typed path), an optional coerce, what it invalidates, and how it interpolates when animated. Callbacks are static by convention (captured once at registration — no per-instance delegate, no reflection).
- **SUIsei.Rect**: An axis-aligned rectangle in pixels — neutral geometry used for layout, hit-testing, clip rects, and draw commands. Stored as origin + size so a zero-size rect is unambiguous; Right/Bottom are derived.
- **SUIsei.RectContent**: A rectangle, optionally rounded, with a fill and an optional border: the Border, Panel and Image primitive. Each is painted by a : a colour, a gradient, or an image (on rounded corners, or as the border, drawn through the vector prim).
- **SUIsei.ResourceDictionary**: A keyed resource store used by and resolved at compile time by the XAML source generator for {StaticResource key} references. Runtime lookup walks in reverse-index order (later entries take priority).
- **SUIsei.RetainedBuffer`1**: A growable array that keeps its storage when cleared: the backing store of a stream rebuilt every frame. It grows by doubling, so a stream that settles at a steady size stops allocating, and its contents are handed out as over the live array rather than copied.
- **SUIsei.RootVisual**: The root of one surface's composition tree.
- **SUIsei.RoutedEvents.CharacterReceivedRoutedEventArgs**: Event args for .
- **SUIsei.RoutedEvents.GettingFocusEventArgs**: Event args for and (both tunnel). Handlers may set to prevent the focus transfer from completing.
- **SUIsei.RoutedEvents.KeyRoutedEventArgs**: Event args for , , and their Preview counterparts.
- **SUIsei.RoutedEvents.PointerPoint**: A snapshot of a pointer at the moment of a routed pointer event — the WinUI PointerPoint, trimmed to what pointer routing needs. On , is in surface pixels; gives it in an element's DIPs.
- **SUIsei.RoutedEvents.PointerRoutedEventArgs**: Payload for the pointer routed events: the and the originating . Pooled by the input pipeline.
- **SUIsei.RoutedEvents.RoutedEvent**: A routed-event identity: a dense assigned at registration, a diagnostic , and the strategy. Registered once in a static field initializer (deterministic, AOT-safe — no assembly scanning), the same self-registration shape as . The dense id keys the per-element handler store with no string lookup.
- **SUIsei.RoutedEvents.RoutedEventArgs**: The base routed-event payload. is the element the event was raised on; is the current element as the route advances; short-circuits the remaining route (a handler that registered handledEventsToo still runs). Mutable + reusable so the input pipeline can pool one instance per dispatch (honouring the "0 GC in the render loop" rule).
- **SUIsei.RoutedEvents.RoutedEventHandler**: The single routed-event delegate shape — typed, so invocation is a direct call with no MethodInfo.Invoke and no argument boxing (the NAOT requirement). The generator wires handlers to it (btn.Click += this.OnClick), signature-checked at generate time.
- **SUIsei.RoutedEvents.RoutingStrategy**: How a travels the element tree. goes root→target (WinUI Preview*), target→root, fires only on the target.
- **SUIsei.Setter**: A single property assignment within a . Writes the Style rung of the DP precedence ladder, so Local values and animations still win over a Style-sourced value.
- **SUIsei.ShapeContent**: A vector shape: a filled and stroked, as WinUI's CompositionSpriteShape draws its geometry. The path is drawn through (a geometry's transform, a shape's stretch), which maps the outline but not the pen. The fill and the stroke are each painted by a : a colour, a linear gradient or an image, measured over . The stroke follows , and draws the part leaves. Retained and versioned like the rest of the composition content. The path, the stroke style and the brushes are retained objects versioned on their own, so a change made inside one of them leaves this content's alone; a compositor keying work on what the shape draws reads their versions too. The tessellations are cached here, keyed by the path (which object, and its version), the path transform, the stroke style's version and the scale bucket the shape is drawn at, so moving, fading, recolouring or trimming a shape never re-tessellates it, and the cache needs no lookup and is collected with the content. A foreign compositor reads the path, transform, paint and style and draws them natively, or takes the tessellation SUIsei's compositor draws from and .
- **SUIsei.ShapeContent.CoverageProbe**: Finds whether any triangle drawn covers a point: the point inside it, and every edge distance interpolated there at least 0.
- **SUIsei.ShapedGlyph**: One positioned glyph produced by an : the atlas to draw, the pen position and per-glyph offsets it sits at (all in EM units, baseline at the origin — the layout scales them by the on-screen font px size), and the source-text (the index of the character it derives from, for caret / hit-test mapping). Whitespace and other zero-geometry glyphs are omitted from a shaped run.
- **SUIsei.Shapes.Ellipse**: An ellipse, as WinUI's Ellipse: the one inscribed in the space it is given, its by default (a circle with ), its stroke inside that space. It asks only for room for its pen, so give it a size or a stretching layout slot.
- **SUIsei.Shapes.Line**: A straight line from (, ) to (, ), as WinUI's Line. It encloses nothing, so it is only stroked.
- **SUIsei.Shapes.Path**: Draws a , as WinUI's Path: , through its . In XAML Data is often path markup, Data="M 0,0 L 10,10 20,0 Z". A change anywhere in the geometry, down to one point, applies in place, as does one to its transform.
- **SUIsei.Shapes.PointOutline**: The outline of a or a : one figure through its points, closed for a polygon, rebuilt in place on the first read after the points or the fill rule change, so moving the points allocates nothing. It is keyed by the collection's own version, so a change made while the shape was not listening (before it joined a live tree) is still seen.
- **SUIsei.Shapes.Polygon**: A closed outline through in turn, as WinUI's Polygon: the last point joins the first. In XAML, Points="0,0 10,5 20,0". A change to the points applies in place; from code, replaces them all with one change and no allocation.
- **SUIsei.Shapes.Polyline**: Straight lines through in turn, as WinUI's Polyline: an open outline, filled as if it were closed. In XAML, Points="0,0 10,5 20,0". A change to the points applies in place; from code, replaces them all with one change and no allocation.
- **SUIsei.Shapes.Rectangle**: A rectangle, its corners optionally rounded, as WinUI's Rectangle. It is sized by the space it is given rather than by an outline of its own: its is by default, and its stroke lies inside that space. It asks only for room for its pen, so give it a size or a stretching layout slot.
- **SUIsei.Shapes.Shape**: The base of the vector shapes, as WinUI's Shape: an outline filled by and stroked by with WinUI's stroke set (thickness, dashes, joins, miter limit and caps), sized by . Every property is a dependency property, so a shape is stylable and its numbers and colours animatable. A shape draws through one retained , which it updates in place when a property changes and never per frame. The tessellation is cached there, so moving, fading or recolouring a shape (its render transform, its opacity, its brushes' colours) costs no layout and no tessellation. While it is in a live tree a shape listens to its brushes, its dash array and its outline's geometry or points, as any element listens to its brushes. Layout. With the outline is drawn in the shape's own coordinates, and the shape asks for the space from its origin to the outline's far edges, the pen included when there is a stroke. Otherwise the outline is scaled into the space the shape is given, half the pen kept inside each edge: in each direction on its own, by the smaller scale and by the larger, keeping its proportions. An outline that does not fill the space is centred in it. The pen is never scaled. A and an are sized by the space itself instead. Hit-testing follows what is drawn: a point hits inside the fill when is set, and on the stroke, within half its thickness of the outline along the dashes, caps and joins it draws, when is. A shape with neither is not hit.
- **SUIsei.SimpleTextShaper**: The default : advance-based, left-to-right, one glyph per code point — no kerning, ligatures, or contextual forms. Each glyph's cluster is its character index. This is the glyph layout a font with no installed shaper uses.
- **SUIsei.Size**: A width/height pair in device-independent pixels (DIPs). Either component may be during measure (an unconstrained axis). Mirrors WinUI's Size.
- **SUIsei.SpriteVisual**: A leaf node that draws : a rect with its border, an image, a glyph run, or a vector shape.
- **SUIsei.Stretch**: How an scales its source into its layout bounds (WinUI Stretch).
- **SUIsei.Style**: An ordered collection of s applied to a via the Style rung of the DP precedence ladder. forms a chain: base setters apply first so derived setters override them. When replaced, the previous style's setters are cleared before the new style is applied.
- **SUIsei.TabFocusNavigation**: Controls how Tab navigation behaves within a subtree (WinUI-compatible).
- **SUIsei.Thickness**: Per-edge spacing in DIPs — used for Margin, Padding, and border thickness (WinUI Thickness).
- **SUIsei.UIDrawList**: A surface's retained draw-list builder — the analog of ImGui's ImDrawList. Bakes the composed transform into vertex positions and merges consecutive primitives that share (kind, texture slot, clip) into one indexed draw command (atlas-everything + state-run batching). It keeps two sets and fills them in turn, so the list it built last stays readable (for damage, and for a host still holding it) while the next one builds, and a surface stops allocating once both sets have grown to its size. Each list is handed out through a ring of reused views. Indices are 16-bit and relative to a window of at most vertices, which each command names by its . When a primitive would not fit in the current window, the open run is flushed at that primitive boundary and continues in a new window starting at the primitive's first vertex, so a surface can hold any number of vertices.
- **SUIsei.UIDrawList.GradientVectorEmitter**: Writes a tessellated path's triangles into the draw list, each cut into the gradient's bands: measured along the line, or along the stroke over length when it is above 0.
- **SUIsei.UIDrawList.KeptVectorEmitter**: Writes a tessellated path's triangles into the draw list, each cut to a box.
- **SUIsei.UIDrawList.VectorEmitter**: Writes a tessellated path's triangles into the draw list, transformed and coloured.
- **SUIsei.UIElement**: The base of every visual element: two-pass measure/arrange, layout invalidation, the owned composition , render-affecting DPs, routed events (pointer + keyboard + focus), hit-testing, and focus/capture queries. The WinUI MeasureCore/ArrangeCore seam lets layer Margin/Min/Max/alignment on top of the element's intrinsic sizing. While it is in a live tree an element listens to the brushes and the transform it shows, so a change to a shared one reaches it on the visual path, with no layout; it stops listening when it leaves, so they do not keep it alive.
- **SUIsei.UIHost**: A per-window UI host — not a singleton, so multi-window/multi-surface is first-class. It owns the input routing and the set of roots outside the render graph, holds no engine or backend handle, and exposes the per-frame split: queue neutral events between frames, then once per frame (drain → hit-test → route → lay out) and (composite each view → ). Both run headless (no GPU), so the whole pipeline is unit-tested by queuing events and asserting DrawLists/DumpState.
- **SUIsei.UILayer**: A screen-space compositing layer for a : sets hit-test priority (higher is on top) and is the DIP→pixel ratio (window DPI/96 for a normal overlay). In-world placement is handled externally by InWorldPanel in Loom.UI.SUIsei, which wraps its own UIHost with a UILayer and projects screen-space pointer events onto the panel's world-space quad — SUIsei itself remains a pure 2D system.
- **SUIsei.UIPrimKind**: The primitive family the UI compositor encodes into a draw command's — it selects the branch the single ui.slang fragment switches on. A flat so it casts to the tag cheaply.
- **SUIsei.UIRoot**: One UI surface: owns the element tree and the composition tree it composites through a pluggable . Holds no engine or backend handle, so + run to completion headless — input crosses in as a size, the product is a neutral (the headless-testable invariant).
- **SUIsei.UISurface**: Well-known s for the UI host. The overlay HUD is list 0; in-world surfaces take higher ids.
- **SUIsei.UIView**: A root handle returned by : the (element + composition trees), its , and whether it is . Keep it to swap the root's content or tear it down. Non-interactive views skip hit-test/focus entirely — useful for pure composites like health bars.
- **SUIsei.VerticalAlignment**: WinUI alignment within a layout slot's vertical axis. fills the slot.
- **SUIsei.Visibility**: WinUI element visibility. contributes zero to layout and never hit-tests.
- **SUIsei.Visual**: A retained composition node — the tree a pluggable renders. Carries a 2D (animatable independently of layout), group , an optional , and a damage flag for incremental recomposition. Backend-neutral.
- **SUIsei.VisualContent**: What a draws: the rectangle family (fill + border, or an image), MSDF glyph-run text, and vector shapes. The compositor switches on the concrete type, with no reflection. Content is retained and mutable, like WinUI's composition objects: an element keeps one content object and updates it in place, so a brush change, an animation frame or a re-arrange allocates nothing. Every change to what it draws advances , which a compositor reads to see what changed and to key work it derives from the content. Whoever changes content marks its visual dirty, as for any other visual change.
